authoring: Hand-authored, in the same convention as ranking-reproducibility-fixtures.json. Every signal below was written by a person to exercise one ranking rule; none was captured from a run, and none carries a department name, a tenant, a provider, a prompt, or any text out of a reader's file. The claims are invented sentences with invented figures. Nothing here is fetched and nothing is stored.
oracle: These fixtures are an ORACLE over src/finops-finding-resolver.js, not a second implementation of it. Each one pins WHICH finding wins, its confidence tier after the provenance rule, its evidence class, the claim template that class selects, and the exact sentence the headline would assert. The ranking rules themselves are asserted nowhere here — a fixture that restated them would agree with a broken resolver.

assumptions.materialityThresholds: The per-kind majorAt values in src/finops-spine-manifest.js: 1 quartile for a peer position, 1 band for a department gap, $5,000 a month for a spend trend or a department driver, $10,000 a month for recoverable spend. ASSUMPTION: a threshold is stated in the kind's own unit because that is the only way a dollar figure and a quartile distance are comparable at all. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE IT: a currency or a period other than USD per month, which would make $5,000 a different size of thing.
assumptions.confidenceLadder: unavailable < low < moderate < high, in src/finops-finding-resolver.js. ASSUMPTION: the index in that list IS the rank, so a downgrade is exactly one step and 'drops a level' has one meaning in this codebase.
assumptions.syntheticDowngrade: A finding drawn from synthetic cohort boundaries loses one level of confidence. ASSUMPTION: a quartile against invented peers is a real comparison against a made-up peer set, and a lead about to repeat it is owed that in the tier and not only in a badge. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE IT: cohort boundaries derived from a measured population, which would be a new provenance kind rather than a change to this one.
assumptions.evidenceClassDefault: Anything not positively marked as the reader's own import is synthetic-cohort evidence. ASSUMPTION: the two errors are not symmetric — understating your own export is a smaller harm than telling a lead they measured something they did not.
assumptions.provenanceTiebreak: Own-export evidence outranks synthetic evidence, but only after materiality, confidence, and the manifest's claim-kind order have all tied. ASSUMPTION: what the finding is worth and whether the page can stand behind it both matter more than whose data it came from.

expected.why: $400 a month is below the $5,000 threshold for a spend trend, so it is minor; two quartiles is at or above the peer position's threshold of 1, so it is major. Materiality is the first rule and it separates them there, before confidence and before provenance. The lead still leads with the synthetic finding, so the entitlement indicator is what stops it reading as measured.

expected.why: The headline may not assert a kind the manifest does not declare, may not assert an empty sentence, and may not assert a claim with no action behind it. The one signal that would have qualified declared itself unavailable, which is skipped rather than rejected — it is not evidence that failed, it is evidence that was not there. With no finding the entitlement slot claims no tier, because a tier for a claim nobody made is exactly the unexplainable number this page must never show.
